newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rice export prices seen rising on demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rice export prices seen rising on demand.

text.p: Pakistani export prices of IRRI-6 variety rice are likely to rise in the next week due to higher demand, exporters said on Thursday.
"We expect a slight rise in the prices of IRRI-6 rice," Javed Islam Agha, chairman of the Lahore-based Rice Exporters Association of Pakistan, told Reuters.
The rise would follow a recent 15,000-tonne deal with a private importer in the Philippines, said Agha.
He said a Pakistani exporter had clinched the deal at $230 per tonne FOB.
The Association held the view that the middle-men in the Philippines were making a lot of money by importing at a cheaper rate and selling in the market at a higher rate, Agha said.
The Association was studying a methodology of selling rice to the private sector in the Philippines at a reasonable price, Agha said.
Another exporter said the prices of super and ordinary varieties of basmati rice, which have a good market in the Gulf, were likely to fall amid low buying interest.
Pakistan exported 1.004 million tonnes of rice worth $279 million in the first eight months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) compared to 828,000 tonnes worth $277 million in the year-ago period.
In February, rice exports rose to 192,976 tonnes worth $47 million compared to 142,317 tonnes worth $36 million in January and 123,707 worth $40 million in February 1996.
